methodological_eligibility.evidence_quote: Once a level and granularity of energy and production data can be selected that demonstrates a clear correlation (linear regression model) then the approach of comparing actual performance versus expected performance becomes possible. This results in a KPI referred to as the Energy Performance Co-Efficient (EnPC).

paper_type.evidence_quote: The energy analysis was completed in a Medical Devices Manufacturing Facility that annually consumes approximately 20 Giga-Watt hours (GWh) of electricity and 15 GWh of natural gas.

ems_standard.evidence_quote: ISO 50001 (ISO, 2011) defines Energy Performance Indicators (EnPIs) as quantitative values or metrics that measure energy performance as defined by the organisation using them.

evidence_quote: Using the linear regression formula, yi = b0 + b1xi, where b0 is the intercept constant (residual) and b1 is the regression co-efficient (slope), the expected energy performance value (E) can be calculated for each weekly production value (P).
Figure 2 shows the Specific Energy Consumption for the available data, i.e. the kWhs per Production Step.

With the development of a clear KPI linking electricity consumption and production activity, historical analysis of the data sets using a Cumulative Sum Control Chart (CUSUM) is possible to demonstrate the changes that have occurred over the period.
